country.name: Namibia

default_in_force_rule.text: Not applied: every version is dated by NamibLII's own expression date, the day the amendment it incorporates took effect as Laws.Africa records it. No date is computed from a default rule.

country.licence_note: Source: NamibLII (https://namiblii.org), licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International licence (CC BY-NC 4.0).

sources.name: NamibLII (Namibia Legal Information Institute: Law Reform and Development Commission, Ministry of Justice, on the Laws.Africa Peachjam platform)
sources.licence: CC BY-NC 4.0, crediting NamibLII as the source (https://namiblii.org/en/terms-of-use/, section 9)
sources.notes: Point-in-time expressions of each act, /akn/na/act/<year>/<num>/eng@<date>. NamibLII's terms prohibit scraping and bulk downloading and its robots.txt sends Content-Signal ai-train=no, so no NamibLII document page was fetched: each expression page is read from an Internet Archive capture (raw id_ form), pinned with its sha256 in sources.json. NamibLII itself was asked only for robots.txt, its terms of use and its open legislation listing page, one per act. Request count covers both.

sources.name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine
sources.licence: Archived copies of NamibLII pages; the content licence is NamibLII's
sources.notes: One CDX prefix listing (namiblii.org/akn/na/act/) for discovery, then https://web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<original url> for the page bytes, through the shared adaptive client scripts/gitlaw_common/wayback.py. Common Crawl was not usable: NamibLII's robots.txt disallows CCBot.

decisions: Acts were chosen by what the archived source supports: every expression NamibLII lists for the Labour Act 2007 (2) and the Companies Act 2004 (3) has a complete Internet Archive copy, so each version is read from its own dated expression.

The Namibian Constitution has one NamibLII expression, 2014-10-13, which takes in the First (Act 34 of 1998, 1998-12-24), Second (Act 7 of 2010, 2010-05-07) and Third (Act 8 of 2014, 2014-10-13) Amendment Acts; NamibLII publishes no earlier expression. The original text (Government Gazette 2 of 21 March 1990) and the three amending Acts exist only as scanned Gazette PDFs (the 1990 Gazette's only text layer is an unreliable OCR layer of the scan), and no OCR is used, so the Constitution's history before 2014-10-13 is not rebuilt: its one version is the oldest available, credited to NamibLII.

The Criminal Procedure Act 51 of 1977 was tried and left out: NamibLII lists 4 expressions (2014-01-01, 2019-01-30, 2023-07-25, 2024-05-15), but every Internet Archive copy of the 2023-07-25 expression is cut off (at 1 MiB) or empty, so the Criminal Procedure Amendment Act 2023's changes could only be dated 2024-05-15, about ten months late.

Licence and terms: NamibLII licenses primary and secondary law content CC BY-NC 4.0, crediting NamibLII as the source; its terms say "Scraping and bulk downloading from this website is strictly prohibited"; its robots.txt sends Content-Signal search=yes, ai-train=no, use=reference and disallows CCBot, ClaudeBot and other AI crawlers. No NamibLII document page was fetched: every version is read from the Internet Archive's copy, through the shared machine-wide rate, for the configured acts only; NamibLII itself was asked only for robots.txt, its terms and one open listing page per act. The user decided on 2026-10-28 that reading these archived copies is acceptable (relayed by the coordinator: "scraping wayback is fair game, dont overdo it"). The repository stays private; CC BY-NC allows only non-commercial use. No legal text was given to a model.
Amending laws carry no enacted or published dates: their NamibLII pages show only the Gazette PDF, so they were not fetched (scripts/africa-law/ISSUES-namibia.md, item 2).
ai_use: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, claude-opus-5-5) wrote the fetch script and configuration and chose the acts. No model wrote, summarised or transformed legal text: parse.py is the shared adapter's deterministic code.
